label: already_ok
evidence: The fix addresses the commit message's race, "arch_busy_wait() is re-entried by two different tasks, the second calling will reset the timer": it removes the write of IT8XXX2_EXT_ETX_COMB_RST_EN that restarted the busy-wait timer on every call, records a start count at entry, and waits on the difference. In ite_it51xxx_timer.c, arch_busy_wait already reads start = read_timer_obser(BUSY_WAIT_H_TIMER) at entry and loops until the difference from start (read_timer_obser(...) - start in count-up mode, start - read_timer_obser(...) otherwise) reaches the wait time, and it writes no timer control register. The only writer of the reset bit TIMER_ETNRST is ext_timer_enable(), which at run time is called only for EVENT_TIMER (timer_driver_set_reload and evt_timer_isr); the busy-wait timers are started once in sys_clock_driver_init via timer_init. A second concurrent caller therefore cannot restart the counter under the first one, so the it51xxx copy never had this race.

label: not_needed_hw
evidence: The H7 fix is about choosing the VCO operation mode (VCOL/VCOH, written with LL_RCC_PLLx_SetVCOOutputRange) together with the input range; per the commit message, the old logic "deduces" the operation mode from input range, which is wrong because "the valid input ranges depend on the selected VCO mode", and the new code also reads the per-product st,vcoh-frequency-range property. The WBA driver has no VCO operation mode at all: set_up_plls only calls get_vco_input_range and LL_RCC_PLL1_SetVCOInputRange, there is no get_vco_output_range and no SetVCOOutputRange call, and get_vco_input_range maps only 4-8 MHz and 8-16 MHz (no 1-2 MHz VCOL range). The repository's WBA PLL binding describes a single PLL with "an input frequency from 4 to 16 MHz" and one VCO range, "VCOx frequency range is 128 to 544 MHz", whereas the H7 PLL binding allows 1 to 16 MHz input and the st,vcoh-frequency-range property exists only in the H7 RCC binding (the WBA RCC binding has no such property). With a single VCO range, selecting the input range from ref_ck alone is correct on WBA, so the mode-deduction bug cannot occur there.

label: already_ok
evidence: The fix is real: per the commit message, the lsm6dsv16x I3C instantiation macro "used the non-existent UNTIL_AND instead of UTIL_AND, making IF_ENABLED silently expand to nothing and dropping the .rtio_ctx, .iodev and .bus_type initializers", so I3C streaming faulted on a NULL RTIO context. In lsm6dsvxxx.c the corresponding macro LSM6DSVXXX_DEFINE_I3C guards both the RTIO definition (LSM6DSVXXX_I3C_RTIO_DEFINE) and the data initializers with the plain IF_ENABLED(CONFIG_I3C_RTIO, ...), with no UTIL_AND/UNTIL_AND combination, so .rtio_ctx, .iodev and .bus_type = RTIO_BUS_I3C are filled whenever the RTIO context is defined. The SPI and I2C variants follow the same pattern with CONFIG_SPI_RTIO and CONFIG_I2C_RTIO, and the string UNTIL_AND appears nowhere under drivers/sensor/st/. The other side never had this typo.

label: not_needed_hw
evidence: The hunk is a real fix: per the commit message, HAL_DFSDM_ChannelInit() 'writes (Awd.Oversampling - 1) into the CHAWSCDR.AWFOSR field and asserts that the ratio is in [1, 32]', and the static DFSDM channel initializer left '.Oversampling = 0'. dmic_stm32_mdf.c drives a different peripheral block: its compatible is st_stm32_mdf (line 6), whose binding is titled 'STM32 MDF (Multi-function Digital Filter)', while the fixed driver binds st,stm32-dfsdm, titled 'STMicroelectronics DFSDM block'. The MDF driver has no DFSDM channel handle, no .Awd initializer and no HAL_DFSDM_ChannelInit() call; it initialises the peripheral with HAL_MDF_Init() (line 659) on an MDF_HandleTypeDef (line 43) whose static initializer (lines 818-837) sets only CommonParam, SerialInterface and FilterBistream. Nothing in the MDF driver configures a watchdog or out-of-limit detector; the only related text is the MDF_ERROR_OUT_OFF_LIMIT case of the error callback, which only logs (line 98). The DFSDM channel register and HAL init contract that the fix depends on therefore do not exist on the MDF side.

label: not_needed_hw
evidence: The hunk is a real fix: the commit message says set_epod_booster() 'divides by PLL1M as well, so with PLL1M > 1 and a source above 16 MHz it picks too small a prescaler', and the fix leaves PLL1M out of the PLL1MBOOST computation. On U5 that code is compiled only under '#if defined(STM32_PLL_ENABLED)' (line 493) and is called from the PLL1 setup path (line 607), where it programs LL_RCC_SetPll1EPodPrescaler() (line 536). The U3 clock driver has no PLL at all: it never references STM32_PLL_ENABLED or STM32_PLL_M_DIVISOR, its SYSCLK can only be MSIS, HSE or HSI (lines 87-91 and 643-653), and the clocks node of dts/arm/st/u3/stm32u3.dtsi (from line 82) defines only hse, hsi, hsi48, msis, msik, lse and lsi, with no counterpart of the U5 'pll1: pll: pll' node of compatible st,stm32u5-pll-clock (stm32u5.dtsi line 141). The U3 booster is set up by enable_epod_booster() (line 336), which selects MSIS as the booster clock source with a fixed /1 prescaler through different LL calls (LL_RCC_SetEPODBoosterClkSource and LL_RCC_SetEPODBoosterClkPrescaler, lines 338-339), so there is no PLL1M divisor in its path to remove.

evidence: The hunks are a real fix: per the commit message, data->accel_freq and data->gyro_freq 'hold the full mode-encoded ODR byte', so using them as a column index into lsm6dsv16x_odr_map[3][13] in the attribute read-back functions lsm6dsv16x_accel_get_config() and lsm6dsv16x_gyro_get_config() 'reads out of bounds for high-accuracy devicetree ODRs'. lis2de12.c has no counterpart of that read-back path: its sensor API (lines 311-318) registers only attr_set, trigger_set, sample_fetch and channel_get, and the driver has no attr_get or get_config function. Its lis2de12_odr_map (line 26) is a one-dimensional table read only inside lis2de12_freq_to_odr_val(), where the index is a loop counter bounded by ARRAY_SIZE (lines 32-33). data->accel_freq is only written (line 91) and is not read anywhere in drivers/sensor/st/lis2de12/, and there is no gyroscope field at all. The out-of-bounds table lookup fixed here therefore does not exist on the lis2de12 side.

label: same_bug
evidence: The hunk is a real fix: per the commit message, max30009_flush_rtio() runs only after the streaming request 'was already completed with rtio_iodev_sqe_ok and data->sqe was set to NULL', so its SQE-acquire-failure branch 'dereferenced NULL'; the fix drops the partially acquired SQEs with rtio_sqe_drop_all() instead. The corresponding adxl367_fifo_flush_rtio() (line 36) is called in the same situation, from the SENSOR_STREAM_DATA_DROP branch of adxl367_process_status_cb() after 'data->sqe = NULL;' (lines 507 and 522-524). It never checks rtio_sqe_acquire() for NULL: it acquires five SQEs (lines 44, 49, 55, 66, 67) from an 8-entry pool (adxl367.c line 1182) and passes each straight to rtio_sqe_prep_tiny_write() or rtio_sqe_prep_callback() (lines 47 and 72), while rtio.h documents that rtio_sqe_acquire() returns NULL when no SQE is available and rtio_sqe_prep_tiny_write() starts with memset(sqe, 0, ...) (sqe.h line 641). So when the SQE pool is exhausted, adxl367 ends the same way max30009 did before the fix, with a NULL dereference in the flush path; the cause differs (no check at all, rather than a NULL request passed to rtio_iodev_sqe_err()), which is why confidence is medium and the port has to be adapted. Nothing ties the fix to hardware or configuration: both drivers use the same RTIO API, and the fix only changes how an SQE shortage is handled.

title: adxl367_fifo_flush_rtio() uses RTIO submission entries without checking that they were acquired, so running out of them dereferences NULL in the FIFO flush path.
summary: Commit 2abd8f6782 (2026-08-20) fixed max30009_flush_rtio(): when it could not acquire RTIO submission entries it reported the error on data->sqe, which is already NULL at that point, and crashed; it now drops the partially acquired entries with rtio_sqe_drop_all(), re-enables the interrupt and returns. The corresponding adxl367_fifo_flush_rtio() runs in the same situation (the DROP branch, after data->sqe has been cleared) but does not check rtio_sqe_acquire() at all: it takes five entries from an 8-entry pool and writes through each pointer straight away. If the pool is exhausted, adxl367 crashes with a NULL dereference instead of logging the failure, dropping the partial entries and re-enabling its interrupt. The patch cannot be copied line for line: adxl367 first needs the NULL checks, then the same rtio_sqe_drop_all() error path. The root cause is not identical to max30009 (no check at all, rather than a wrong pointer inside the check), and pool exhaustion is an uncommon condition, so a human should confirm that this counts as the same problem.
